name: Meltano
license: MIT (the Meltano Singer SDK is Apache 2.0); the managed Meltano Cloud is proprietary
summary: A command-line ELT tool that runs Singer taps and targets from a `meltano.yml` project kept in git.
intro: Meltano is a Python CLI, not a server. A project is a directory with a `meltano.yml` file that lists plugins and their settings: extractors (Singer “taps”), loaders (Singer “targets”), mappers, and utilities such as dbt. `meltano add` looks a plugin up on MeltanoHub, which catalogues more than 600 connectors, and installs it into its own Python virtual environment. `meltano run tap-github target-duckdb` starts both programs and pipes one into the other: the tap prints Singer messages (`SCHEMA`, `RECORD` and `STATE`) as JSON lines and the target loads them. Meltano saves the last `STATE`, by default in a SQLite system database under `.meltano/`, or in S3, GCS or Azure Blob Storage for throwaway runners, and hands it back on the next run so only new data is read.

Meltano is free under the MIT licence. It has no scheduler of its own: `meltano schedule` hands schedules to an orchestrator plugin, usually Airflow, or you call `meltano run` from cron or CI. New connectors are usually built with the Meltano Singer SDK. The project now belongs to Matatika, a London data company that sells a managed Meltano Cloud priced by compute hours (Starter includes 200 a month, Growth 2,000, Scale 5,000), with prices given on request.
strengths: Pipelines as code: `meltano.yml`, named environments such as dev and prod, and changes reviewed in pull requests
Reuses the Singer ecosystem: 600+ taps and targets on MeltanoHub, often in several maintained variants
Light to run: one pip-installable CLI that works on a laptop, in CI or in a container, with no service to keep up
The Singer SDK makes a new REST, GraphQL or SQL tap a small Python project
Plain MIT licence on the core
limits: Connector quality varies: many taps are community-maintained, a source may have several competing variants, and fixing one is often on you
Every record passes as a JSON line through a pipe, which suits SaaS APIs but is slow for big database copies; the faster `BATCH` message is optional per connector
No UI or scheduler in the open-source tool: the web UI was removed in 3.0 (2023), so you need Airflow, cron or a paid cloud
Ownership has changed three times: GitLab, then Meltano Inc. (renamed Arch Data in 2023), then Matatika in 2026; the first Meltano Cloud was shut down in 2024 in favour of Arch
Python packaging: each plugin gets its own virtual environment, and Meltano 4 needs Python 3.10 or later

snippet.title: Copy GitHub issues into DuckDB with a Meltano project
source: meltano add tap-github target-duckdb        # both land in meltano.yml
meltano config set target-duckdb filepath output/warehouse.duckdb
meltano config set target-duckdb default_target_schema raw
export TAP_GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN=ghp_...         # secrets stay out of meltano.yml
meltano run tap-github target-duckdb        # state is saved; the next run is incremental

items.name: Singer spec
items.text: Taps write `SCHEMA`, `RECORD` and `STATE` messages to stdout; targets read them from stdin. Any language works, so `tap | target` is a pipeline.

items.name: MeltanoHub
items.text: Lists 600+ extractors, loaders, mappers and utilities, with each variant’s settings, so `meltano add` knows how to install and configure them.

items.name: Meltano Singer SDK
items.text: A Python framework that handles the spec, state, schema flattening and stream maps, so a new tap or target only describes the source or destination.

items.name: Meltano Cloud
items.text: Matatika’s managed service runs projects from your Git repository with schedules, retries and support, billed by compute hours rather than rows.

story: Meltano began inside GitLab in 2018. GitLab’s data team wanted one tool for the whole lifecycle (the name stands for model, extract, load, transform, analyze, notebook, orchestrate), because, as the announcement put it, connecting Salesforce and Marketo to judge a campaign was “non-trivial”. Version 1.0 shipped in October 2019.

In 2020 the team narrowed the goal to an open-source platform for ELT pipelines built on Singer, the tap-and-target spec that already had dozens of community connectors but no answer for deployment, configuration or keeping state. In 2021 they released the Singer SDK and MeltanoHub, and on 30 June Meltano spun out of GitLab with a $4.2M seed round led by GV, Douwe Maan as CEO.

At the end of 2023 Meltano Inc. renamed itself Arch Data and built Arch, a data platform for software teams, on top of Meltano; Arch replaced the managed Meltano Cloud. Arch later shut down, and by January 2026 the London company Matatika had acquired the Meltano project and relaunched Meltano Cloud.

choices.choice: Adopt Singer rather than invent a connector format
choices.why: Singer already had a community and dozens of taps and targets. What it lacked was tooling to configure, deploy and track state, which Meltano could add.
The team came from GitLab and wanted data work to use software habits: code review, environments and CI/CD instead of settings clicked into a UI.
Taps and targets are separate Python packages that pin conflicting library versions, so each is installed in isolation.

timeline.text: Refocused on open-source ELT built on Singer taps and targets
Singer SDK and MeltanoHub launch; spins out of GitLab with GV seed
Meltano 3.0 drops the web UI; Meltano Inc. renames itself Arch Data
Meltano 4.0 adds structured logging and needs Python 3.10+
Matatika acquires Meltano after Arch shuts down; Meltano Cloud returns
